subject: Request: Edge-region replication window — SLA carve-out and interim RTO/RPO
messages:
From: James Holloway <james@edgeops.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@edgeops.com, procurement@fincloud.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Edge-region replication window — SLA carve-out

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we prepare for go-live with several latency-sensitive customers (financial exchanges and ad partners), we ran one more risk review on our end. We use a narrow set of edge POPs in us-west for primary inference and rely on asynchronous replication to the nearest regional standby. That replication pipeline has an operational window where in-flight KV state can lag by up to ~25 minutes during large spine rebalances.

We understand Redwood's standard multi-region SLA targets 99.99% availability with an RTO of 5 minutes and RPO of 0 (no data loss) for primary regional failover. For our environment we need a short carve-out: an interim RTO of 15 minutes and an RPO of 30 minutes for the us-west-edge replication window for the first 90 days after go-live, while we complete the cross-region streaming hardening plan.

Are you able to review this exception and outline what operational guardrails (metrics, runbooks, compensating controls) you would require to approve? Attached is a short design doc that explains the replication topology and the proposed mitigations.

We are under a procurement timeline and would appreciate a response this week so we can finalize the contract language.

Thanks,
James Holloway
Director, Platform Engineering
EdgeOps Inc.

Attachments: replication-design.pdf (12 KB)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: James Holloway <james@edgeops.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Edge-region replication window — SLA carve-out

Hi James — thanks for the clear summary and the design doc. I appreciate the timeline pressure.

Quick answer: we can consider a time-limited carve-out provided a set of compensating controls are in place and we get sign-off from infra/ops and Legal. To move fast, here's what we need from you by EOD Wed:
- Confirm the exact list of edge POPs (example: us-west-edge-1, us-west-edge-2) and expected peak write rate.
- Provide the runbook for manual failover and the test playbook you will run before go-live.
- Agreement to the observability hooks we require (token-level trace for the replication stream, 1-min delta metrics).

If you can provide those, I'll coordinate an internal assessment with Neha (security/procurement) and Vivek (infrastructure). Assuming no blockers, we can send a draft carve-out clause and a 90-day interim SLA proposal for review.

Thanks — I'll also attach a draft clause (sla-carveout-draft.docx) and our proposed monitoring checklist.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 415 555 0192

Attachments: sla-carveout-draft.docx
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: EdgeOps carve-out request — quick notes

Rachel/Vivek — looping in my notes after reviewing James' design and the replication metrics: 

1) Risk assessment summary: Acceptable for a short, monitored carve-out. Key conditions:
   - 90-day limit and automated re-eval at 30/60 days.
   - Customer to enable the tracing hooks and agree to an SLO degradation alert that auto-triggers a canary rollback.

2) Technical constraints:
   - The replication gap described (up to ~25m) is consistent with our observed overflow windows for high-shard churn. We can mitigate via a temporary buffered write queue and a conservative failover policy.

3) Proposed interim SLA (internal draft):
   - Availability: 99.95% for the edge-region during the carve-out period.
   - RTO: 15 minutes maximum for failover to regional standby.
   - RPO: 30 minutes maximum acceptable data lag.
   - Operational requirements: daily replication delta report for first 14 days, then every 48 hours.

4) Legal / Contract asks for Rachel to get confirmation from EdgeOps that procurement will accept a clause that includes an explicit remediation plan and a limited credit schedule capped at 25% of one month of usage for events tied solely to edge replication lag.

I suggest we prepare a short customer-facing note summarizing the above and circulate the carve-out clause to Legal. Vivek — can you confirm feasability of the buffered queue approach and whether it requires any infra changes on our side?

-Neha

On Wed, Oct 21, 2026 at 09:12 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> We'll need a small feature flag toggle and an extra autoscaler rule for the standby instances to ensure cold-start cost doesn't spike during a 15 minute RTO window. I estimate 3 engineer-days to ship the toggle and tests.
>
> - Vivek
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: James Holloway <james@edgeops.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Edge-region replication window — SLA carve-out

James — thanks for the follow-up materials and for turning the runbook around quickly. Per our internal review (Neha and Vivek), Redwood can approve a time-limited carve-out under the following terms: 

Summary of agreed interim carve-out (90 days):
- Availability target for us-west-edge: 99.95% (measured at route level)
- RTO: 15 minutes maximum for failover to regional standby
- RPO: 30 minutes maximum allowable replication lag
- Monitoring & reporting: daily replication-delta report for first 14 days, then every 48 hours; 1-min delta metric streamed to our tracing endpoint.
- Operational controls: customer to run the attached failover test playbook before go-live; Redwood will run a canary swap during low-traffic windows and reserve the right to pause failover if delta > 45 minutes.
- Credits: for incidents attributable to this carve-out, credit schedule capped at 25% of one month of usage (limited to replication-window failures)

Next steps / action items:
1) EdgeOps to countersign the attached carve-out clause and return to contracts@redwood.com (please include the procurement contact).
2) EdgeOps to provide the final edge POP list and peak write rate (James) by EOD Thu, Oct 29.
3) Redwood infra (Vivek) to enable the temporary autoscaler toggle and deployment of the buffered write queue (ETA: 3 business days after code freeze).
4) Joint canary test schedule: propose Nov 3–5 for the first controlled failover; Redwood will send a calendar invite once we receive the signed clause.

I've attached the redlined carve-out for your signature (sla-carveout-draft.docx) and the replication metrics we used for our assessment (cross-region-latency-metrics.csv). If that looks good I'll ask Legal to produce the final DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 415 555 0192

Attachments: sla-carveout-draft.docx, cross-region-latency-metrics.csv
